title: Almost-Sidon Sets with One Collision
description: Max size of A ⊆ {1,...,N} with at most one sum collision? Conjecture: (1+o(1))·(2/√3)·√N. Erdős-Freud (1991) matched this with a reflected Sidon construction.

sections.title: Module Header: Almost-Sidon Problem, Key Results, and Imports
sections.summary: Module docstring for Erdos Problem #864: maximum size of A in {1,...,N} with at most one sum collision. Lists five key results: Erdos-Freud lower bound (2/sqrt(3))*sqrt(N), the matching upper bound conjecture, the difference version sqrt(N), the Sidon baseline sqrt(N)+O(N^{1/4}), and connection to Problem #840. Imports Mathlib.Data.Finset.Basic and Mathlib.Tactic; opens Finset.
sections.mathContext: An almost-Sidon set allows exactly one repeated pairwise sum. The Sidon condition (0 collisions) gives |A| <= sqrt(N) + O(N^{1/4}) via double counting differences. The reflected construction B union (N-B) with Sidon B in {1,...,N/3} achieves approximately (2/sqrt(3))*sqrt(N) — a 15.5% improvement — since B in {1,...,N/3} ensures the only collision is at sum N.

sections.title: Core Definitions: sumRepCount, multiRepSet, IsAlmostSidon, IsSidon
sections.summary: Defines sumRepCount A n as the number of pairs (a,b) in A with a <= b and a+b = n (filtered Cartesian product), multiRepSet A as {n : sumRepCount >= 2}, IsAlmostSidon A as |multiRepSet A| <= 1, IsSidon A as |multiRepSet A| = 0, and maxAlmostSidon N as the supremum over almost-Sidon subsets of Icc 1 N.
sections.mathContext: sumRepCount uses Finset.filter on A x A restricted to pairs with a <= b to avoid double-counting. IsAlmostSidon/IsSidon are cardinality predicates on multiRepSet — existential-free characterizations of the collision condition. maxAlmostSidon N is a Finset.sup over the powerset (computable but expensive for large N).

sections.title: Known Bounds, Axioms, and Basic Theorems
sections.summary: Axiomatizes the Erdos-Freud lower bound (exists B almost-Sidon in [1,N] with |B| >= (2/sqrt(3) - e)*sqrt(N)), the Sidon upper bound (|A| <= sqrt(N) + N^{1/4}), and almost_sidon_exceeds_sidon. Proves sidon_is_almost_sidon by omega, isAlmostSidon_empty, isAlmostSidon_subset, and isSidon_empty.
sections.mathContext: sidon_is_almost_sidon: IsSidon A implies IsAlmostSidon A follows immediately since |multiRepSet A| = 0 implies |multiRepSet A| <= 1 (omega). isAlmostSidon_subset: if B is almost-Sidon and A is a subset of B, then multiRepSet A is a subset of multiRepSet B (monotone), so |multiRepSet A| <= |multiRepSet B| <= 1. The Erdos-Freud lower bound is axiomatized as it requires the full Singer/Sidon construction analysis.

sections.title: Structural Properties, Difference Counting, and Sidon Bounds
sections.summary: Major proof section: pairwise_sum_count (|A|*(|A|+1)/2 sums bound), sum_in_range, isSidon_subset, distinct_sums_bounded, sidon_counting_bound, sidon_card_sq_le, and the difference counting improvements. Key achievement: sidon_diff_counting_bound and sidon_card_sq_le_2N prove the Sidon upper bound via difference counting, eliminating the sidon_upper_bound axiom.
sections.mathContext: The difference counting approach (sidon_diff_counting_bound): if A is Sidon in [1,N], all differences a-b (with a > b) are distinct, giving |A|*(|A|-1) <= N-1 non-zero differences, thus |A|^2 <= |A| + N - 1 <= 2N for N >= 1. This stronger approach eliminates the sidon_upper_bound axiom, reducing the file from 2 to 1 axioms.

sections.title: Reflected Construction: Validity Proof and Quantitative Lower Bound
sections.summary: The largest section (300 lines): reflected_construction_valid proves that B union (N-B) is almost-Sidon when B is Sidon in {1,...,N/3}. The proof analyzes collision structure showing any repeated sum must equal N (the only cross-pair collision from b+(N-b)=N). Closes with reflected_construction_bound: maxAlmostSidon N >= 2*|B| for any Sidon B in {1,...,N/3}.
sections.mathContext: The reflected construction B union (N-B): for B Sidon in [1,N/3] and b in B, N-b lies in [2N/3, N-1] disjoint from B. Cross-pair sums: b + (N-b') = N only if b = b' (since B is Sidon). Same-side sums from B are distinct (Sidon property). Same-side sums from N-B: (N-b) + (N-b') = 2N - (b+b') are also distinct (Sidon). So the only repeated sum is N, confirming at most one collision.

overview.historicalContext: Sidon sets (also called $B_2$ sets) are sets where all pairwise sums are distinct, studied since Sidon's 1932 question to Turán. The classical result is $|A| \leq \sqrt{N} + O(N^{1/4})$ for Sidon $A \subseteq \{1, \ldots, N\}$, with matching constructions from finite geometry (Singer 1938, Erdős-Turán 1941). Problem 864, posed by Erdős and Freud in 1991, asks: what happens if we relax the Sidon condition to allow exactly one collision? They showed the reflected construction $B \cup \{N - b : b \in B\}$ with Sidon $B \subseteq \{1, \ldots, N/3\}$ achieves size $(2/\sqrt{3})\sqrt{N} \approx 1.155\sqrt{N}$, a 15.5% improvement over pure Sidon. The only collision occurs at sum $N$: both $b + (N-b)$ and $b' + (N-b')$ equal $N$. The conjecture that this is optimal remains open. This is a weaker version of Problem #840, which studies the general $k$-collision case.
overview.problemStatement: What is the maximum size of $A \subseteq \{1, \ldots, N\}$ such that at most one integer $n$ has multiple representations as $a + b$ with $a \leq b \in A$?
overview.text: Max size of A ⊆ {1,...,N} with at most one sum collision? Conjecture: (1+o(1))·(2/√3)·√N. Erdős-Freud (1991) matched this with a reflected Sidon construction.
overview.proofStrategy: The formalization defines sum representations via filtered Cartesian products, the almost-Sidon and Sidon properties via cardinality of the multi-representation set, and `maxAlmostSidon` as a supremum over the powerset. The key theorem `sidon_is_almost_sidon` is proved by unfolding definitions and `omega`. Asymptotic bounds are axiomatized with explicit real-valued inequalities using `Real.sqrt`.
keyInsights: Almost-Sidon allows one collision; the reflected construction achieves $2/\sqrt{3} \approx 1.155$ times the Sidon bound by concentrating all collisions at a single sum value $N$

The reflected construction $B \cup (N - B)$: when $B$ is Sidon in $\{1, \ldots, N/3\}$, the set has size $\approx 2\sqrt{N/3} = (2/\sqrt{3})\sqrt{N}$, and the only collision is at sum $N$ since $b + (N-b) = N$ for all $b \in B$

The naive sum range bound $k(k+1)/2 - 1 \leq 2N - 1$ is FALSE: counterexample $A = \{1,2,4,6,7\} \subseteq [1,7]$ has collision multiplicity 3 at sum 8. The correct bound accounts for collision multiplicity $c$: $k(k+1)/2 - (c-1) \leq 2N - 1$
The gap between Sidon ($\sqrt{N}$) and almost-Sidon ($(2/\sqrt{3})\sqrt{N}$) is precisely the factor $2/\sqrt{3}$: one collision is worth a multiplicative factor of $\approx 1.155$
For differences instead of sums, Erdős-Freud proved the maximum is asymptotically $\sqrt{N}$ — the difference version does not benefit from allowing one collision

conclusion.summary: Erdős Problem #864 is formalized with concrete definitions of sum representation counting, almost-Sidon and Sidon properties, the maximum function, and the Erdős-Freud reflected construction. The key theorem sidon_is_almost_sidon is proved; bounds and construction validity are axiomatized. The file has 0 sorries and 3 axioms. The false axiom almost_sidon_sum_range was identified and removed (counterexample: A={1,2,4,6,7}, N=7).
conclusion.implications: A resolution would precisely quantify the value of allowing one sum collision in additive combinatorics. The factor 2/√3 would establish a sharp phase transition: zero collisions gives √N, one collision gives (2/√3)√N, and understanding k collisions would complete the picture of B_2^+ set theory.
openQuestions: Is |A| ≤ (1+o(1))·(2/√3)·√N the correct upper bound for almost-Sidon sets?
What is the maximum for k allowed collisions? Is there a formula f(k)·√N?
Is the reflected construction the unique extremal configuration, or are there essentially different constructions?
What is the connection to Problem #840 (general collision bounds)?

crossReferences.description: Problem #840 studies the general $k$-collision case (quasi-Sidon sets with at most $k$ collisions); #864 is the special case $k = 1$, asking for the maximum size of a set with at most one repeated pairwise sum

Problem #30 defines Sidon sets (0 sum collisions) and establishes the classical bound $|A| \leq \sqrt{N} + O(N^{1/4})$. Problem #864 relaxes the Sidon condition to allow one collision, asking whether the $\sqrt{2/3}$ improvement factor from the reflected construction $B \cup (N - B)$ is optimal

Problem #329 studies the maximum density of Sidon sets in $\{1, \ldots, N\}$. Problem #864 extends this to almost-Sidon sets (one collision), where the conjectured maximum $(2/\sqrt{3})\sqrt{N}$ exceeds the Sidon bound $\sqrt{N}$ by the factor $2/\sqrt{3} \approx 1.155$

Problem #862 studies maximal Sidon subsets — Sidon sets that cannot be extended. Problem #864's almost-Sidon sets represent a controlled relaxation: allowing exactly one collision enables larger sets while retaining most of the sum-distinctness structure

Problem #757 studies Sidon sets within families that are almost-Sidon. Both explore the transition zone between exact Sidon sets and their relaxations, with #864 quantifying the size gain from allowing one collision and #757 asking how large a true Sidon subset of an almost-Sidon family can be
